subject: ela
intro: When you read informational text and find a word you do not know, you can use context clues — the other words and sentences around the unknown word — to figure out its meaning. Look at what the sentence says, think about what makes sense, and look for nearby definitions or explanations. Content-area words (science, history, geography) often have clues nearby.

items.prompt:
Read the article below.

Owls are nocturnal animals. They sleep during the day and come out to hunt at night. Their large eyes help them see in the dark.

What does the word 'nocturnal' mean as used in the passage?

steps: I find the word 'nocturnal' in the text.
I read the sentence and the sentences near it for clues.
The next sentence says: 'They sleep during the day and come out to hunt at night.'
This tells me nocturnal animals are active at night, not during the day.
So 'nocturnal' means active at night.
solution.answer: 'Nocturnal' means active at night and asleep during the day.

items.prompt:
Read the article below.

Volcanoes erupt when pressure builds up underground. The hot, melted rock that flows out is called lava. After lava cools, it hardens into solid rock.

What does the word 'erupt' mean as used in the passage?

steps: I find the word 'erupt' in the first sentence.
The sentence says volcanoes erupt 'when pressure builds up underground.'
The next sentence describes hot melted rock flowing out after this happens.
I can infer that 'erupt' means to burst or explode, releasing material from inside.
So 'erupt' means to burst open and shoot out lava and gas.
solution.answer: 'Erupt' means to burst open and shoot out hot melted rock and gases.

items.prompt:
Read the article below.

Bees are important pollinators. When a bee visits a flower to collect nectar, tiny grains of pollen stick to its body. The bee carries the pollen to other flowers, helping them grow seeds.

What does the word 'pollinators' mean as used in the passage?

steps: I find the word 'pollinators' in the first sentence.
The rest of the passage explains what bees do: they carry pollen from flower to flower.
So a 'pollinator' is something that carries and moves pollen.
'Pollinators' are animals that carry pollen from one flower to another, helping plants reproduce.
solution.answer: 'Pollinators' are animals, like bees, that carry pollen from one flower to another, which helps plants grow seeds.

items.prompt:
Read the article below.

Many birds migrate when the seasons change. Migration means traveling from one place to another in search of food or better weather. Geese, for example, fly south in autumn and return north in spring.

What does the word 'migrate' mean as used in the passage?

steps: I find the word 'migrate' in the first sentence.
The next sentence gives a direct definition: 'Migration means traveling from one place to another in search of food or better weather.'
This tells me 'migrate' means to travel from one place to another with the seasons.
So 'migrate' means to travel to a different place when seasons change, to find food or better weather.
solution.answer: 'Migrate' means to travel from one place to another when seasons change, in search of food or better weather.

items.prompt:
Read the article below.

The ocean floor has different zones. The deepest zone is called the abyss. It is completely dark, extremely cold, and under tremendous pressure. Very few creatures can survive there.

What does the word 'abyss' mean as used in the passage?

steps: I find the word 'abyss' in the second sentence.
The next sentence describes the abyss: 'It is completely dark, extremely cold, and under tremendous pressure.'
The passage also says it is the deepest zone.
So 'abyss' means the deepest, darkest part of the ocean.
Combining clues: 'abyss' refers to the deepest, darkest part of the ocean.
solution.answer: 'Abyss' means the deepest, darkest zone of the ocean, where there is no light and the pressure is very high.

items.prompt:
Read the article below.

Deserts are arid environments. They receive less than 10 inches of rain per year. Because of the lack of water, only specially adapted plants and animals can survive there.

What does the word 'arid' mean as used in the passage?
items.hint: Look at what the next sentence says about deserts and rain.

steps: The next sentence says deserts receive less than 10 inches of rain per year.
A place with very little rain would be dry.
So 'arid' means very dry, with very little rainfall.
solution.answer: 'Arid' means very dry, receiving very little rain.

items.prompt:
Read the article below.

A caterpillar goes through a process called metamorphosis. It starts as an egg, then becomes a caterpillar, then forms a chrysalis, and finally emerges as a butterfly. This amazing transformation happens inside the chrysalis.

What does the word 'metamorphosis' mean as used in the passage?
items.hint: Look for clues in the words 'process' and 'transformation.'

steps: The passage says metamorphosis is a 'process' and describes it as an 'amazing transformation.'
It then lists the stages: egg, caterpillar, chrysalis, butterfly.
A transformation through stages means a big change in form.
So 'metamorphosis' means a series of changes in form that an animal goes through.
solution.answer: 'Metamorphosis' means the series of changes in form that an insect goes through as it grows, such as from egg to caterpillar to butterfly.

items.prompt:
Read the article below.

The tundra is a vast, cold, treeless plain found in the Arctic. The ground is frozen for most of the year. Only small plants like mosses and grasses can grow there.

What does the word 'tundra' mean as used in the passage?
items.hint: The passage gives a description right after the word 'tundra.'

steps: The word 'tundra' is followed by a description: 'a vast, cold, treeless plain found in the Arctic.'
So 'tundra' is a type of landscape.
'Tundra' means a large, cold, treeless area of land in the Arctic.
solution.answer: 'Tundra' means a large, cold, flat, treeless area found in the Arctic region.

items.prompt:
Read the article below.

Some animals are predators, meaning they hunt and eat other animals. Lions, hawks, and sharks are all predators. The animals they hunt are called prey.

What does the word 'predators' mean as used in the passage?
items.hint: Look for the definition clue in the same sentence as the word 'predators.'

steps: The sentence gives a direct definition: animals that 'hunt and eat other animals.'
Lions, hawks, and sharks are examples.
So 'predators' means animals that hunt and eat other animals.
solution.answer: 'Predators' are animals that hunt and eat other animals.

items.prompt:
Read the article below.

Earthworms are decomposers. They eat dead leaves and plants, breaking them down into tiny pieces. This releases nutrients back into the soil, which helps new plants grow.

What does the word 'decomposers' mean as used in the passage?
items.hint: What do earthworms do to dead leaves and plants? Use that to figure out what decomposers are.

steps: The passage says decomposers 'eat dead leaves and plants, breaking them down into tiny pieces.'
This releases nutrients back into the soil.
So 'decomposers' are living things that break down dead plant and animal material.
solution.answer: 'Decomposers' are living things that break down dead plants and animals, releasing nutrients back into the soil.
